title: Persuasive Impact: Result vs Intended Effect

sections.content:
You know *tan … que*, *tanto … que*, *de tal manera que* and *de tal modo que* with the indicative for real results from B2 Unit 31. In persuasive rhetoric, however, *de tal modo que* and *de tal manera que* carry a sharp mood contrast.

Use the **indicative** when reporting an **achieved factual result**: *habló de tal modo que cautivó al auditorio* ('he spoke in such a way that he captivated the audience'). Use the **subjunctive** when giving advice or stating an **intended rhetorical purpose**: *ordene sus ideas de tal modo que el público las recuerde* ('arrange your ideas so that the audience remembers them').

For rhetorical climax, speakers also use *hasta tal punto que* + indicative ('to such an extent that'): *la historia conmovió a la sala hasta tal punto que el aplauso duró un minuto*.

sections.title: Indicative vs subjunctive after *de tal modo que*
rows: *Expuso el caso de tal modo que persuadió a la sala.*
*Estructure la charla de tal modo que capte la atención.*
*Conmovió al público hasta tal punto que nadie interrumpió.*

items.spanish: El orador moduló la voz de tal modo que cautivó a toda la sala.
items.english: The speaker modulated his voice in such a way that he captivated the whole room.

items.spanish: Prepare el cierre de tal manera que el público recuerde una sola idea persuasiva.
items.english: Prepare the closing in such a way that the audience remembers a single persuasive idea.

items.spanish: El relato conmovió a los asistentes hasta tal punto que el aplauso fue inmediato.
items.english: The story moved the attendees to such an extent that the applause was immediate.

items.spanish: Debemos hablar de tal modo que nuestra persuasión nazca de la claridad.
items.english: We must speak in such a way that our persuasion springs from clarity.

sections.content: Check whether the sentence reports what **actually happened** (indicative: *habló de tal modo que convenció*) or prescribes an **intended effect** (subjunctive: *hable de tal modo que convenza*). Never write *de tal modo a que* — there is no *a* before *que*.
